Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers:
- Private Offer CTA: the product detail page supports both a \"Request Private Offer\" CTA and a direct \"Buy (Private Offer)\" CTA depending on whether the offer is pre-configured. For buyer-facing copy we recommend keeping the CTA to 3–5 words; longer explanatory text should live in the short description area.
- Copy constraints: no explicit claims about third-party certifications (e.g., \"SOC 2 certified\") unless you link to evidence in the listing. Max hero title length ~120 characters; short description ~400 characters.
- DocuSign/process link: Marketplace does not host DocuSign links directly; you can link to an external URL in the private offer flow. For Private Offers you supply the terms and the offer URL; when the buyer accepts in Seller Center the order is generated.

Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/ (seller docs).

If you'd like, we can review the final wording once updated. Please also provide the private offer SKU and partner friendly URL when ready.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Seller Support
marketplace-seller-support@amazon.com

Kimberly / Lukas — I spoke with Sarah on a quick call this morning. Procurement at ACME is expecting:
- Standard AWS private offer flow, plus ACME legal will request a redline against our standard enterprise MSA (they typically push a 45–60 day review cadence).
- Pricing visibility: they want the private offer to show the net price and the SKU code in the buyer portal so their internal approvers can map costs into their chargeback system.
- Billing: ACME prefers invoicing via AWS (Marketplace billing).

Implications for copy: add one procurement snippet that says \"Private offer presents net price and SKU code in buyer portal for internal approvals.\" Also flag that we should add a short footnote about expected legal review timing (45–60 days).
